A 2024 list of operational systems names a Children's Court case management system; with the Judiciary's e-filing notices current to October 2025, the cell reaches stage 4.

Rebuild: The 2025 state budget funds an integrated information and document system that the common-jurisdiction courts were to start in 2025 (AGO-001), so a system is being built. No source says it is in service in any court, so not stage 3.

Rebuild: In October 2026 the justice sector presented the planned E-Justice platform, being prepared with UNDP support to keep judicial case files (BDI-001, BDI-002), so a system is being built. Nothing says it is in service.

Rebuild: An e-justice information system for criminal and civil procedures was at feasibility study in 2024 (BEN-001), so it is under way. Online filing at the Cotonou commercial court (BEN-004) cannot count while no case management system is shown in service.
Rebuild: A 2025-2027 project to digitise the criminal and administrative judicial chains has a development team at work (BFA-001), so a system is being built. Nothing says it is in service.
Rebuild: The Industrial Court has developed an electronic case management system with a soft launch planned for mid-2026 (BWA-001), so it is being built. No source says it went live.

Rebuild: The e-justice.ci platform reaches all 39 first-instance courts, but what it serves is certificates and criminal records (CIV-001); the minister's promise to digitise all judicial procedures (CIV-004) is work under way. No source says courts manage cases on it, so not stage 3.
Rebuild: CMR-001 dates from January 2023, outside the window, and no later row says anything on the questions. Unplaced.

Rebuild: UNDP says SIGAJ, a judicial case management system, was introduced in the justice sector by 2024 (COD-002), so case management is in service. Commercial-court and interconnection work (COD-001, COD-003) is under way, and nothing says cases can be filed online.

Rebuild: Law 38/X/2024 says the Justice Information System has been phased in over a decade for electronic handling of cases in the courts, though its mass use is hindered (CPV-001), so it is in service in some courts. Nothing says cases can be filed online.
Rebuild: UNDP reports a pilot digital case management system for minor offences under construction in 2024 (DJI-001), so it is being built. Nothing says it is in service.

Rebuild: The national electronic window lets parties follow their cases from any administrative court (DZA-002), so the administrative courts manage cases electronically. Each step must be met: no source says cases can be filed online, so case tracking and judgments online (DZA-001) cannot lift it to stage 5.

Rebuild: The E-Court platform launched in August 2026 serves certified digital copies of case files and hearing decisions by SMS (EGY-001, EGY-002), so case management is in service in the criminal courts. Nothing says lawyers can file cases online.
Rebuild: ERI-001 is a 2001 evaluation, outside the window, and no later row says anything on the questions. Unplaced.

Rebuild: The Federal Supreme Court planned eCourt pilots from September 2025, with INSA building the court management information system (ETH-001), so it is being built. No source says it is in service.

Rebuild: A December 2025 report says eJustice is still being rolled out and the IMF called it stalled (GHA-001), so it stands as under way. The 2022 case count (GHA-002) is outside the window and cannot show it in service now.

Rebuild: A consultancy signed in September 2026 is to set up the Conakry commercial court's integrated management system (GIN-002), and a private firm has digitised that court's roll and decisions (GIN-001), so work is under way. Nothing says a case management system is in service.

Rebuild: The electronic case management system was in pilot in August 2024 (GMB-005), the Chief Justice still awaited its implementation in January 2026 (GMB-002), and a tender to build an integrated system followed in March 2026 (GMB-001). It is piloted, not in service, so stage 2; the e-filing the NHRC names (GMB-004) cannot count above that.
Rebuild: The Supreme Court and UNDP agreed in October 2024 to digitise case files in three courts, with a first payment for equipment (GNQ-001), so work is under way. Nothing says it is in service.

Rebuild: The Case Tracking System runs registry operations (KEN-002), e-filing reached every court in March 2024 (KEN-001, KEN-003), and the Causelist Portal lets anyone find when and where a case is heard (KEN-004). Every step is met, so stage 5.

Rebuild: The Judiciary's 2026-2030 Strategic Plan, backed by the Finance Minister in July 2026, is to put an electronic case management system in all circuit courts (LBR-001). That is a plan with funding, so stage 2 at most.

Rebuild: The Chief Justice said in July 2026 that the Judiciary is implementing digital systems including electronic filing (LSO-001), and the 2024 rules provide for e-justice from a date not yet gazetted (LSO-002). Work is under way; nothing says a system is in service.

Rebuild: Lawyers file briefs and appeals through a dedicated platform (MAR-003), and the national enforcement platform is in service and being extended (MAR-007). The public file tracking on Mahakim (MAR-005) carries only the year 2026, so it is not yet counted and the cell stays at 4.

Rebuild: The Justice Ministry said in June 2026 that case tools such as LogiCivil and LogiPenal are deployed in the courts (MDG-001), so case management is in service. Nothing says cases can be filed online.

Rebuild: The e-Justice platform is being put into operation with UNDP equipment, first for certificates and criminal records, with case processing to follow (MLI-001, MLI-003). That is under way; nothing says courts manage cases on it.

Rebuild: A November 2024 government list names a case management system in service for the Children's Court (MUS-005), so stage 3. The online-filing rule (MUS-001) dates from January 2021, outside the window, and no row since November 2023 says lawyers file online, so not stage 4.

Rebuild: The Judiciary's April 2024 concept note says digital case management platforms have already been introduced (MWI-002), so stage 3. Its e-court with electronic filing was a pilot in ten courts (MWI-001), which does not show lawyers filing online.

Rebuild: In July 2025 the Chief Justice said the Supreme Court is entirely on paper and that work to extend e-justice to it is under way (NAM-001, NAM-002). The 2018 description of eJustice in the High Court (NAM-005) is outside the window, so stage 2.

Rebuild: The Nigerian Case Management System went live at the Supreme Court on 1 July 2026 (NGA-001), and practice directions require counsel to upload processes and records of appeal to it (NGA-003). That is filing online; nothing says the public can look up cases.

Rebuild: The upgraded integrated case management system is in use from January 2025 (RWA-001), and the October 2026 Governance Scorecard rates electronic court filing services (RWA-002). Nothing says judgments or case status are open online.
Rebuild: SDN-001 and SDN-002 are from 2016, outside the window, and no later row says anything on the questions. Unplaced.

Rebuild: The programme's final report records the e-Justice platform deployed in one court with five procedures digitised (SEN-004), and it was launched officially in September 2026 (SEN-001), so it is in service in some courts. Nothing says cases can be filed online.
Rebuild: SLE-001 is dated 2022 and SLE-002 2017, both outside the window, so neither can set a rung. Unplaced.

Rebuild: The Justice Sector Integrated Electronic Case Management System was launched in October 2025, linking police, prosecutors, courts and prisons in one electronic workflow (SOM-001), so it is in service. Nothing says cases can be filed online.
Rebuild: The justice ministry was working with a contractor in 2024 so that court cases can be processed electronically (STP-001), so a system is being built. Nothing says it is in service.
Rebuild: The IECMS was launched in August 2025 with user training and is being rolled out (SWZ-001, SWZ-002). No source says courts already manage cases on it, so stage 2.

Rebuild: The Judiciary launched phase one of its e-Service Platform in November 2025, the first of a phased digital rollout (SYC-003), so an e-justice system is being built. Online filing (SYC-001) cannot count while no case management system is shown in service.
Rebuild: The justice ministry launched a digital exchange platform with UNDP in October 2025, piloted in N'Djamena (TCD-001), so a system is piloted. Nothing says courts manage cases on it.

Rebuild: The Lome commercial court runs SYSCOM for its cases (TGO-002, TGO-004), lawyers file pleadings through it online (TGO-003), and since July 2026 the Lome high court's portal lets parties follow procedures remotely (TGO-001). Every step is met, so stage 5.

Rebuild: The African Development Bank notice of September 2025 is for a contract to build an e-Justice portal and business application (TUN-001), so it is being procured. The 2023 Jshare pilot is outside the window.

Rebuild: The electronic case management system is in service from the Court of Appeal to district courts (TZA-003, TZA-004), litigants file cases online (TZA-005), and they can track a case's progress online (TZA-006). Every step is met, so stage 5, as Uganda and Zimbabwe on the same kind of fact.
Rebuild: ECCMIS is in more than 56 courts (UGA-010), cases are filed and fees paid online (UGA-008), and litigants check their case files on it by phone (UGA-009). Every step is met, so stage 5.

Rebuild: Court Online is in service in 19 High Court seats (ZAF-001), and practitioners and litigants upload process for issue on it (ZAF-003, ZAF-005). Nothing says the public can look up a case or that judgments are published online.

Rebuild: Treasury funds an electronic case management system being developed for all court levels, the Judiciary still working by hand in January 2025 (ZMB-001), so stage 2. The 2022 report of a stalled system and decisions online (ZMB-002, ZMB-003) is outside the window.

Rebuild: The IECMS runs in the Constitutional, Supreme, Labour and High Courts (ZWE-001), litigants and practitioners file on it (ZWE-003), and court users can track their cases (ZWE-004). Every step is met, so stage 5.
